mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates and reduced corporate borrowing, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25pp over prior month, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.5%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that suppresses corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances with FEDFUNDS > 3.5%, or signal's Rank IC is negative over 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in FEDFUNDS and declines in UNRATE indicate an overheating economy where aggressive policy tightening outweighs labor market strength, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative return prediction fails when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, with SPX 20-day returns positive in >55% of cases, or interaction term p-value >0.05 in regression.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >55% of periods with PAYEMS increase >100k, or Rank IC <0.02 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In low-unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), further declines in unemployment signal wage inflation pressures that trigger premature central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of periods with UNRATE < 4.0%, or signal's Rank IC is negative over 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1,500,000 units (HOUST > 1500.0) signal strong consumer demand and economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >55% of periods with HOUST > 1500.0, or Rank IC <0.02 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output and economic activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods with INDPRO increase >0.5% over prior month, or Rank IC <0.02 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust consumer spending and housing market strength, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days through earnings momentum.
failure_condition: Positive return prediction fails when RSAFS and HOUST both rise >0.5%, with SPX 60-day returns negative in >55% of cases, or interaction term p-value >0.05 in regression.
